clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy Supraspinatus Impingement evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy Supraspinatus Impingement is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes first-line physical therapy and activity modification, reserving imaging for suspected full-thickness tear or failed conservative care, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: painful arc of motion between 60 and 120 degrees when reaching overhead and pain sleeping on shoulder with positive Neer test

Key HPI features: 55M painter presenting with a 2-month history of anterolateral shoulder ache, worse with overhead reaching and when lying on the shoulder at night, with positive Neer/Hawkins impingement signs and pain on empty can testing without drop arm on exam.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals normal. Painful arc of abduction between 60-120 degrees. Positive Neer and Hawkins impingement signs. Positive empty can (Jobe) test reproducing pain without frank weakness; no drop-arm sign. Full passive range of motion. No visible atrophy, AC joint non-tender. Normal cervical spine exam.
Relevant background/PMH: No significant chronic medical history
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy Supraspinatus Impingement.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe progressive motor deficit.
management_principles: Begin first-line conservative treatment: activity modification, NSAIDs, and a structured physical therapy program focused on scapular stabilization and rotator cuff strengthening for 6-12 weeks
Consider a subacromial corticosteroid injection for persistent pain limiting participation in therapy
Reserve imaging (ultrasound or MRI) for suspected full-thickness tear (positive drop arm, significant weakness), failure to improve after 6-12 weeks of conservative therapy, or acute trauma
Refer to orthopedics for surgical evaluation if a full-thickness tear is confirmed or conservative treatment fails.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 55M painter presenting with a 2-month history of anterolateral shoulder ache, worse with overhead reaching and when lying on the shoulder at night, with positive Neer/Hawkins impingement signs and pain on empty can testing without drop arm on exam.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Painful arc of abduction between 60-120 degrees. Positive Neer and Hawkins impingement signs. Positive empty can (Jobe) test reproducing pain without frank weakness; no drop-arm sign. Full passive range of motion. No visible atrophy, AC joint non-tender. Normal cervical spine exam.
reference_soap.assessment: Rotator cuff tendinopathy with subacromial impingement (supraspinatus), clinical diagnosis without evidence of full-thickness tear.
reference_soap.plan: Begin first-line conservative management: activity modification, NSAIDs, and a structured physical therapy program focused on scapular stabilization and rotator cuff strengthening for 6-12 weeks. Consider a subacromial corticosteroid injection for persistent pain. Reserve imaging for suspected full-thickness tear or failure to improve, and refer to orthopedics for surgical evaluation if conservative treatment fails.

teaching.one_liner: Physical medicine presentation involving painful arc of motion between 60 and 120 degrees when reaching overhead and pain sleeping on shoulder with positive Neer test.

must_ask.say: Did the shoulder pain start after a lot of overhead reaching or activity, like painting?
Is the pain worst in a specific range when you lift your arm, like between shoulder and ear height?

must_ask.objective: Night pain when lying on shoulder
must_ask.say: Does the pain wake you up at night, especially when lying on that shoulder?
Do you feel true weakness lifting your arm, or is it mainly pain stopping you?
Have you tried any physical therapy, rest, or injections, and what activities are you hoping to get back to?

history.answer: My right shoulder has been hurting whenever I try to lift my arm up or reach for things overhead.
It is just my right shoulder, right on the front and side of the joint. None of my other joints hurt.
It started gradually about two months ago and has been slowly getting more noticeable.
It feels like a deep, dull ache most of the day, but it turns into a sharp pain around a 6 out of 10 when I lift my arm high.
The pain catches sharply when my arm is halfway up, between shoulder level and my ear, but if I push through past that it actually hurts a bit less.
It definitely flares up when I reach above my head, like when I am painting high ceilings or reaching into top cabinets.
Yes, it wakes me up at night whenever I roll over onto my right side, so I have to sleep on my left side or my back.
I can still hold my arm up once it gets there, but the sharp pain makes it feel weak when I try to push or lift things.
No, I have not noticed any swelling, redness, or heat in the shoulder.
No, I do not have any morning stiffness in the joint. It is just stiff for a few minutes if I accidentally laid on it.
Lifting my arm out to the side or overhead makes it much worse, while resting my arm down by my side eases the ache.
Walking and using stairs are completely fine, but reaching overhead at work and putting on a jacket have become tough.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or sweats.
No, I did not fall or wrench it, and I did not hear any popping sound. It just crept up from repetitive work.
I have had mild soreness after heavy painting jobs before, but it always went away in a few days. It has never lasted months like this.
No, I have not felt unusually tired, and my weight has been completely steady.
No rashes, no scalp issues, no mouth sores, no eye redness, and no dry eyes or mouth.
No, I do not have any morning back stiffness, heel pain, or swelling in my fingers or toes.
No recent diarrhea, no pain with urination, and no recent sore throat or cold.
I do not eat excessive red meat or seafood, I drink only occasionally, and I do not take water pills.
No, I have never taken steroid pills, and I have never had any injections or surgery on this shoulder.
I have been happily married for twenty-five years with no other sexual partners.
I was hoping to get a cortisone shot right into the joint and some quick exercises so I can finish painting this house by Friday.
I figured I just pinched a tendon or wore down the joint from holding heavy paint rollers over my head all day.
I'm really worried this will need surgery, because being off work for months would completely bankrupt my independent painting business.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or arthritis.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications or regular supplements.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I might have one beer on a weekend, but nothing more than that.
I work full-time as an interior and exterior painter, and I live with my wife in a single-story home.
There is no family history of joint diseases, rheumatoid arthritis, or early degenerative conditions.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
A well-developed man sitting comfortably in no acute distress, with no visible muscle wasting, deformity, or asymmetry around the shoulder girdle.

Active abduction shows a painful arc between 60 and 120 degrees, with positive Neer and Hawkins impingement signs, full passive range of motion, and no warmth, swelling, or acromioclavicular joint tenderness.
Positive empty can test reproducing anterolateral shoulder pain without true weakness, negative drop arm sign, and 5/5 strength throughout the rest of the upper extremity.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation across both upper extremities, including the lateral deltoid area.
Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Full cervical spine range of motion without midline tenderness, and negative Spurling test bilaterally.
No erythema, psoriatic plaques, subcutaneous tophi, or nail pitting observed.
